doc.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Serge Chaloff throws his baritone book in the river; Gene Ammons's memory
summary: Story of Serge Chaloff being fired by Woody Herman and throwing away the book he had memorized; Gene Ammons also had a photographic memory.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Yeah, in fact I hear stories about guys who used to accidentally lose parts from things that got too difficult.

Oh yeah. You remember the famous baritone player Serge Chaloff, he played with Woody Herman. Well Serge was a wonderful baritone player but he memorized the whole book. But he had a habit of coming to work late or coming back after the intermission too late, and Woody was getting sick of it, and told him next time you’re going to get fired, next time you’re late. And Serge showed up late and Woody fired him right there, or gave him his two weeks’ notice. So the bus was traveling you know. And so they were crossing a bridge over a river, so Serge took his book, the baritone book and he flung it out the window into the river, and he looked at Woody and says, “You can’t fire me.” He says, “I got it all up here.” And he did. He knew every part. And there are some players that are like that. I remember Gene Ammons was like that. I mean not as far as being late, but I mean as far as they have a photographic memory. Gene Ammons, we played in a local big band called Jimmy Dale’s big band in Chicago. And Gene would just look at the music once and he’s got every note up there. And he concentrated then on phrasing. So he became as important to the reed section as the lead alto player. In fact even the lead alto player, they’d want to follow his leading because he would have the right inflections or the right spirit. And so like I say Serge was like that too. He told him, “You can’t fire me.” And he couldn’t until somebody copied the book again or wrote the parts out, and that took a while, because they had a book like it was that thick.
That was nasty. I think I heard a follow up or something about Woody Herman getting back to him, something in the Bill Crow book. Pretty nasty actually.
Something about using his leg as a urinal or something.
Yes. Yeah that’s true. It was a bar or something. I heard that that was a true story.
